items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I’ll go listen to Charlie Parker you know or Trane or I mean, we all have influences.

ctx.x: I just — you know what it’s like, I love I appreciate, like we said there’s so many great musicians who know every Paul Chambers solo and John Coltrane solo and can play fast and do this and that. I’m always impressed. But when I hear a musician, whether it be bass or anything, who, they play some, it may be simple, it may even be bad, but I can tell they thought it up, like I can tell it’s from them. It’s organically from them, or that they believe it. That means a lot and I think the audience knows that. And I…
a bunch of Israel Crosby shit that’s influenced by him. But I don’t know, I just try to be honest. And I think the audiences feel that.
